subject: Predict existing model on new data

messages.author: 812cd10215f6d9ef
messages.subject: Predict existing model on new data
parts:
I performed a confirmatory factor analysis to test whether variables could be reduced in latent constructs. I also performed a measurement invariance test to investigate whether the model was also applicable to another group of participants. At this moment I have data from a few participants from other groups. This is not enough yet to perform another measurement invariance test, but I would like to predict scores on latent constructs also for these participants (assuming at this moment that this model is also applicable to those grous). Is it possible to predict scores on an exisiting model without changing the parameters at this point? 

I hope I made my question clear enough... 

Thanks in advance, 

Marjanneke de Jong

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Predict existing model on new data
parts:
I would like to predict scores on latent constructs also for these participants (assuming at this moment that this model is also applicable to those groups). Is it possible to predict scores on an exisiting model without changing the parameters at this point? 


The predict function accepts an argument called "newdata" for lavaan objects, just as it does for other model classes (e.g., lm, glm).

findMethods(predict, classes = "lavaan")

Just submit a data.frame of your new observations (which must at least include each of the observed variables in the original model) to the predict function, and it returns factor scores for each "newdata" observation

> example(cfa)
...
> dat <- data.frame(t(colMeans(HolzingerSwineford1939[,paste0("x", 1:9)])))
> dat
       x1      x2       x3       x4       x5       x6       x7       x8       x9
1 4.93577 6.08804 2.250415 3.060908 4.340532 2.185572 4.185902 5.527076 5.374123
> predict(fit, newdata = dat)
     visual textul speed
[1,]      0      0     0

Terry
